shorts.title: What you will learn: Default arguments and overloading
shorts.hook: Many functions can share one name.
shorts.script: Many functions can share one name. Today we give functions more flexibility. They get default values, and they can share a name. A default argument is a value that the compiler uses when the caller leaves it out. Overloading means several functions share one name, but have different parameters. The compiler picks the one that matches the call best. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

shorts.title: Bug of the Day: An ambiguous call
shorts.hook: Can you spot the bug in default arguments and overloading?
shorts.script: Can you spot the bug in default arguments and overloading? Bug of the Day. We call show with the plain number five. There is a long version and a double version. The compiler says the call is ambiguous. An int fits both equally well. Write five with the letter L, or add an int version. An int converts to long and to double with the same cost, so the compiler cannot choose. Keep coding, says Xecxec!
